page.layout: Running head at top centre; page number at top right. Below them, two round coin medallions side by side, each with a legend. Below the medallions, one column of running text in two paragraphs, with the gathering signature at the right after the text. A small woodcut ornament sits at the bottom centre, with no text.

main_text.l: D.N. CONSTANTIVS P.F.AVG
IMP.C. CONSTANTINVS.III
CONSTANS, devicto fratre Constantino, omni cona-
tu superatis Alpibus Galliam intrat, varióq; eventu biennio pu-
gnans, patre fratris in potestatem redigit. Primùm agit bonum
principē, mox sive adversa valetudinē, sive rerum prosperitate
mutatus, ingratus omnibus esse coepit, donec & ipse Magnen-
tij dolo, quem etiam servaverat, dormiēs[?] intra tentorium, non
longe ab Hispaniis, ad Helenam oppidum, opprimitur, anno
ætatis 30. Imperij 13. Consulito Pomp. Læt. & Bap. Egna. li.1.
CONSTANTIVS, cædem fratris Constantis ulturus,
magno exercitu adversus Magnētium cōparato, ingenti illum
prælio, & memorabili, ad Murtiū, sive Mursam, vicit, quo Ro-
mani vires Imperij penè cōciderē, 53. millibus utrinque defide-
ratis. Mox cum Magnentius bellū reparasset, & ad Lugdunum
iterum victus esset, gladio sibi latus aperuit. Cæterùm Cōstan-
tius, iterum in Persas cōtendens, dum ægrè fert Iulianum à mi-
litibus Augustū esse dictum, iuxta Tauri mōtis radices æstuan-
tissima febre correptus, moritur, anno ætatis 40. Imperij 2 4.
Hic orbis dominum se vocavit:Iulianum adoptavit. Consulito
autores quos supra.

page.notes: Two coin medallions (engravings) at the top, showing laureate busts facing right; their legends are transcribed above as lines. Woodcut ornament at the bottom centre, not transcribed. The "dormiēs" word is uncertain: the tilde over the e is hard to read at this scan resolution. The running head is transcribed with its printed full stop.
